scenes.shot: The slide on the canvas, the pointer reading down it; 'One unfamiliar word goes by, and you're lost.' beside it
scenes.say: Some of the most interesting ideas in the world are explained in rooms most of us can't follow. A research talk. A paper. A lecture. One unfamiliar word goes by, and you're lost.

scenes.shot: The climb card fades in over the canvas, then away
scenes.say: Looking it up usually makes it worse. The definition is written in words even more specialized than the one you didn't know. You climb, when you needed to descend. And ten tabs later, you've lost your place.

scenes.shot: A box is drawn around 'Biot–Savart law'; the card lands beside it
scenes.say: Librarian is a research librarian on an infinite canvas. Put the thing that stopped you on the canvas, a slide, a page, a paper, and draw a box around the part you don't understand.

scenes.shot: The card builds section by section as each is named, gliding to the middle
scenes.say: It explains downward, toward what you already know. First why the idea exists, then what it is, then its parts, then how it's used right here. It's drawn as a diagram, not a wall of text, so you can see how the pieces connect.

scenes.shot: Close on the marked terms and stand-ins
scenes.say: It's honest about language. Strict technical terms are marked as strict. Everyday words standing in for a technical one say which one they mean. You always know which words are loose.

scenes.shot: Words selected in the card; a new card opens to the right
scenes.say: Still stuck? Select any words in the explanation and go one level further down. Each detour becomes a new card, right beside the one it came from.

scenes.shot: The plus on a piece opens the palette; a shape grows
scenes.say: Or grow the diagram itself. Ask why. Ask for the steps. Break a piece into its parts, or see it two ways. Each new piece can grow again, as deep as you want to go.

scenes.shot: Zooming out over a whole canvas
scenes.say: Nothing ever moves on its own. Every question you asked stays where you asked it, so the way back is always one look away.

scenes.shot: A lecture plays on the canvas; Stop; the frame and transcript land beside it
scenes.say: It works with lectures too. Watching a video and something loses you? Stop it. The exact frame, and what the lecturer was saying, land on the canvas, ready to ask about. Then jump straight back to where you were.

scenes.shot: Found sources and the course chips on a card
scenes.say: Every explanation is grounded in sources it went and found. And it notices where an idea is usually taught, an intro course or a graduate seminar, so it can keep things at your level.

scenes.shot: A Wikipedia article on the canvas, drawn as shapes, then section by section
scenes.say: Bring a whole page, and it keeps all of it. A long article is redrawn section by section, every fact, date and name carried over. Nothing is summarized away. And a page anyone has read before opens instantly.

scenes.shot: On a call: words selected, said aloud; the answer, and a shape grown where they pointed
scenes.say: Or just talk to it. Start a call, keep your hand on the page, select the words that lost you, and say: this part, right here. It answers out loud, and changes the canvas as it talks. It grows the piece you mean, or goes and finds you videos.

scenes.shot: A notebook opens beside the canvas, credited to where it was found, and runs
scenes.say: Want to see it actually work? Ask for an example in a notebook. It finds a real one, written and run by a real person, keeps the cells that matter, and credits where it came from. Then it runs, right there in your browser.

scenes.shot: A card's chat asks for university lectures; the gallery, each video with its channel
scenes.say: Ask a card for whatever you need, in your own words. Videos, reading, papers. It doesn't just take the top search results. It checks who made each one, so asking for university lectures gets you lectures from universities.

scenes.shot: A plot read with the cursor, a graph rearranged by hand, a table charting itself, a map going to a place
scenes.say: Or ask for a figure. Equations get plotted. How the ideas connect becomes a graph you can rearrange. Data comes back as a table, read off real pages and credited, and it charts itself. And places land on a real map, placed by a real map service, not by guesswork.

scenes.shot: The Goals panel opens; a goal lights its cards; a subgoal walks to its card
scenes.say: As you go, it keeps track of what you're after. Each card is filed under your goal, under something that goal turned out to need, or as a side trip. So three detours deep, the way back to what you wanted is right there.

scenes.shot: On a call: pointing at Berlin on the map; then 'the chart' is numbered three ways, and one is picked
scenes.say: On a call, it knows what you're pointing at, even a city on a map. And when it isn't sure what you mean, it doesn't guess. It numbers the choices, and you just say which.
Librarian. Free, open, and no account needed. Bring the thing that stopped you.
